sourceName: Walmart Supercenters with reported overnight-parking tolerance (CA/NV trip corridor)
method: Two passes. (1) LOCATION: every store named Walmart within ~20 mi of the real captured route anchors was pulled from OpenStreetMap via the Overpass API (bbox queries over the Ventura -> Grapevine -> I-5 -> Sacramento -> US-50/I-80 corridor), which carries Walmart's own store number in ref:walmart plus street address and opening_hours. A second hyphen-tolerant pass (name~'Wal.?[Mm]art') over the central I-5 box 35.05/-120.90 to 37.60/-119.60 confirmed no store was missed. Gaps were double-checked against Nominatim for Coalinga, Avenal, Kettleman City, Lost Hills, Buttonwillow, Firebaugh, Dos Palos, Gustine, Newman, Lathrop, Auburn, Colfax, Truckee and South Lake Tahoe -- all returned no Walmart. (2) POLICY: each candidate was checked against AllStays' California and Nevada 'No Parking Walmart Stores' lists (community-report and signage based, 249 CA + 35 NV entries) and against its own AllStays per-store page, which carries dated first-hand parking reports. City ordinances were checked where the store-level picture was ambiguous. Coordinates here are OSM building centroids, never estimated from a city name.
policyNote: Walmart corporate has no overnight-parking policy to cite: permission is per-store manager discretion, subject to local law. On THIS corridor the result is close to a blanket no. Of ~30 Walmarts within 10 miles of the route, all but two appear on AllStays' community-compiled no-overnight-parking list, and the per-store reports repeatedly describe posted 'no overnight parking' signage, tow warnings, security sweeps and phoned-in refusals (Manteca, Stockton x2, Tracy, Patterson, Placerville, Elk Grove, Rancho Cordova, North Highlands, Santa Clarita, Ventura, and every Reno/Sparks/Carson City store). Several CA cities also prohibit the activity itself rather than the parking: Sacramento City Code 12.52.030 (unlawful camping, reaching private as well as public property), Rancho Cordova RCMC 9.85 ('No person shall camp anywhere in the city ... whether on public or private property'), and Los Banos Municipal Code Title 9 Ch. 3 Art. 20 Pt. 3, which makes it unlawful between 10:00 p.m. and 6:00 a.m. to occupy any motor vehicle 'upon any lot, piece or parcel of land within the City' for sleeping quarters. The Los Banos and Sacramento ordinance texts are quoted here from search-engine excerpts of ecode360/qcode pages; the primary pages are Cloudflare-blocked and could not be fetched directly, so treat the exact wording as second-hand. Net effect: this category is nearly useless on the I-5 Central Valley run and should not be relied on to close that gap. Only two records are shipped, both with caveats stated in full below. Every excluded store is documented in the curation report rather than padded into this file.

records.name: Walmart Supercenter -- Los Banos (W Pacheco Blvd)
records.source: AllStays store #2117 parking reports (community-submitted); location and store number from OpenStreetMap way 311712102
records.notes: DOWNGRADED TO UNVERIFIED 2026-08-12 by the integrating session: the research note itself rates confidence MEDIUM-LOW, the three first-hand reports disagree, and a citywide ordinance may prohibit vehicle sleeping here outright -- that is not 'confirmed policy', which is what verified:true means in this schema. Kept as a pin because it is the only option in a 175-mile dead zone, but it must not read as confirmed. Same standard applied to South Lake Tahoe, where a comparable ordinance meant shipping no pin at all. The ONLY Walmart within 10 miles of the route anywhere in the 175-mile I-5 dead zone between the Grapevine and Patterson -- at every route anchor from mile 126 to mile 250 the nearest Walmart is 21 to 40 miles away, over on CA-99. This one sits about 6 miles off the route line, on CA-152 (W Pacheco Blvd) east of I-5. EVIDENCE CONFLICTS AND YOU SHOULD KNOW IT: May 2023 a traveller asked customer service and was told 'Yes, certainly' and called it the nicest Walmart overnight they could recall, with lots of tree shade in a huge lot; March 2023 someone stayed in an RV alongside another rig without asking; but April 2023 a camper-truck driver phoned and was told 'No overnight allowed.' Two of three signals are positive and no one has reported signage or a tow warning here -- it is one of only two corridor stores absent from AllStays' no-parking list. Against that: Los Banos Municipal Code (Title 9, Ch. 3, Art. 20, Pt. 3) reportedly makes it unlawful to occupy a vehicle for sleeping on ANY parcel in the city between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m., which would cover this lot regardless of what the store says; that text is second-hand via search excerpts, not a page I could fetch. Practical: store hours are 06:00-24:00, NOT 24 hours, so go inside and ask before midnight or you have no one to ask. Park toward the shaded outer edges away from the entrance, arrive late, leave early, buy something. CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM-LOW. Real, specific, first-hand evidence exists, but all of it is roughly three years old and it disagrees with itself, and the city ordinance is a genuine legal risk rather than a theoretical one. Treat as a fallback, not a plan.

records.name: Walmart Supercenter -- Sacramento (Delta Shores)
records.source: OpenStreetMap way 545766729 (store #2464) for location; policy status unresolved -- absent from AllStays' CA no-overnight-parking list and has no AllStays store page
records.notes: VERIFIED FALSE ON PURPOSE: the store is real and the coordinate is a genuine OSM building centroid, but I found NO trustworthy signal either way about its overnight policy -- no dated visitor reports, no signage reports, no store page on AllStays. It is included only because it is the last Walmart near the route that is not affirmatively flagged as prohibited, which is different from being known-good. Absence of evidence is not permission: AllStays itself says its no-parking list is incomplete. This is a newer Supercenter (opened in the Delta Shores development) about 5.6 miles off the mile-375 route anchor, just off I-5 at Cosumnes River Blvd on the south edge of Sacramento -- large, flat, well-lit lot shared with the wider retail centre. Working against it: Sacramento City Code 12.52.030 (unlawful camping) reaches private property, and every other Sacramento-area Walmart on this corridor -- Florin Rd, Gerber Rd, Delta Shores' neighbours in Elk Grove, Rancho Cordova, North Highlands, Citrus Heights, Antelope, West Sacramento -- is on the no-parking list. Call 916-665-1011 and ask the manager before you commit; store hours are 06:00-24:00, so ask before midnight. CONFIDENCE: LOW -- location confirmed, policy entirely unknown.
